In luring free agents, the A’s will face one more season in a AAA park and are coming off of 98 losses no matter how they came by it. Payroll may be increasing but is not going to rival the top 10 spenders. The bigger free agent deals are known to generally be unwise investments and this off-season most everyone is seeking starting pitching creating a “player’s market”. So to land someone worth getting excited about, you probably have to accept a player-friendly deal that wipes out much of your existing payroll flexibility for a contract you will later regret. It’s basically “a more expensive Luis Severino”. In terms of trade, in order to add meaningful starting pitching the A’s would almost certainly have to part with a current key position player, e.g., Shea Langeliers, Tyler Soderstrom, Zack Gelof, or a coveted minor leaguer expected to contribute mightily to the team as soon as 2028, e.g., Leo De Vries, Jamie Arnold, Drew Burress. Perhaps the best bet is an MLB-ready SP not yet proven, the next Dan Haren — who could also be the next Dan Meyer, an equally touted pitcher only he got hurt and was never the same. The type of pitcher the A’s may well have targeted when they were at AAA would be, I don’t know, Luis Morales and Jack Perkins? Long term, Smith and Castro figure to greatly improve the A’s pitching through enhancement of the very way they draft, develop, and train pitchers from the ground up. But whether they can spin their magic to turn the current group into gems, whether they can bring in enough talent move the needle in the coming year — you might need Anne Sullivan for that and she’s been, er, retired for 90 years.

item.title: Dolphins fan confidence climbs following Lions game, ahead of Week 10 at Colts
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 08: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins in action against the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have won just one game over the first nine weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Having already passed their bye week, the Dolphins are 1-7, which would typically lead to a frustrated fanbase itching for change. This year, for the Dolphins, however, the fans seem to be accepting that this is only the first season of a long-term rebuild, understanding that losses now may lead to victories in the future. Things are not all well in Miami, though. This week, two major pieces of the starting lineup landed on injured reserve. Quarterback Malik Willis heads to the sideline for at least four weeks with a groin injury; season-ending surgery hasn’t been ruled out, but there is hope he can return in a few weeks. The news was not as good for defensive tackle Zach Sieler, who tore his biceps muscle last week. The injury occurred on the first snap of Miami’s game against the Detroit Lions, but the veteran played through it for the rest of the game. Now he will undergo surgery and will need around six months of recovery time before he is cleared to return to football activities. Miami faces the Indianapolis Colts tomorrow as the NFL’s Week 10 schedule continues. Despite Indianapolis struggling this year, earning just two wins against seven losses in the first half of the season, the oddsmakers see the Colts still likely to win this game. The latest FanDuel Sportsbook odds have the Colts favored by 3.5 points over Miami. Dolphins fan confidence The highlight of the season for the Dolphins came in Week 7, when they beat the New York Jets. Our Week 8 SB Nation Reacts fan confidence survey reflected the victory with a 97 percent positive rating for the Dolphins. It was the high-water mark of the year, and the only week in which our survey topped the 90 percent mark. At least until this week. Going toe-to-toe with the Detroit Lions for much of Week 9 encouraged the fans that brighter days are coming. The survey opened before the news of the injuries to Willis and Sieler broke, but then ran throughout the rest of the week, and it remained up above 90 percent all week. When the poll closed, 91 percent of the responses indicated the Dolphins are headed in the right direction. How will tomorrow’s game against the Colts affect next week’s survey? We will be back early next week to ask for your updated confidence in Miami’s direction. item.title: Mavericks Streak Ends In 39-Point Blowout As Defense Collapses
item.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Dallas Mavericks saw their three-game winning streak end in a crushing defeat on Thursday night at Target Center. Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball and backup Bones Hyland combined for 11 three-pointers as the Timberwolves scored 133 points to beat Dallas 94. This loss dropped the Mavericks to a 7-5 record and marked their worst performance of the season by a wide margin. Coach Dusty May admitted after the game that his team could not match the intensity of the Minnesota squad. The Timberwolves dominated the paint with 74 points and forced 19 turnovers from Dallas. This loss highlighted major issues with Dallas defense and ball handling that will require immediate attention from the coaching staff and players alike. Minnesota Defense Disrupts Every Dallas Play The primary reason for the loss was the aggressive pressure applied by the Minnesota defense. Dallas coach Dusty May stated that the Timberwolves were extremely disruptive with their point of attack defense and activity on and off the ball. He noted that Minnesota deserved to win the game based on their defensive effort alone. The Timberwolves entered the game ranked first in the league for defensive efficiency, allowing only 106.1 points per 100 possessions. Dallas struggled to get clean catches against this pressure, especially in pick-and-roll situations. According to Synergy Sports data, the Mavericks earned just 0.524 points per possession when Minnesota kept one defender on the ball handler. This pressure forced Dallas into 19 turnovers, with 10 of those coming directly from steals. The Timberwolves also blocked seven shots and held Dallas to just 37.2 percent shooting from the field. May explained that the team speed and intensity of Minnesota made it difficult for Dallas to sustain any offensive rhythm. He pointed out that having two rim protectors behind the perimeter defenders was a luxury that Dallas could not overcome. The Mavericks failed to make enough better screens or increase their pace to counteract the defensive schemes used by the Timberwolves throughout the night. Cooper Flagg And Kyrie Irving Struggle To Score Key Dallas players Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving combined for only 22 points on 9-of-23 shooting during the game. The quiet performance in Minneapolis was especially disappointing for these two players, who had combined for 78 points three nights earlier in a win over the Indiana Pacers. Irving recorded a minus-36 rating, which was the worst mark on either team and reflected the struggles of the Mavericks while he was on the court. Neither player saw action in the fourth quarter as the game was already out of reach. May observed that Minnesota possessed a single body before crossing half-court, a circumstance that stopped Dallas from utilizing that focus to create offensive opportunities in other areas. The lack of scoring from these primary options forced other players to step up, but the overall team shooting remained poor.

item.title: Football pitch ruined by 'selfish' vandals in car
item.description: Bispham Junior Football Federation said their children's football pitch had been ruined by vandals [LDRS] A football pitch has been ruined by "selfish" vandals in a car, a youth team has said. Bispham Junior Football Federation in Blackpool said a vehicle was seen driving around in circles on to the pitch on Wednesday night before a person got out and tore up the grass. Chairman Lisa Hannigan said the club was due to host matches on the pitch on Saturday and Sunday, but they had to be moved due to the unplayable state of the turf. "We don't know if they intentionally set out to damage the pitch but it looks that way," Hannigan said. "It makes me angry to think someone could be so selfish and not consider the implications of their actions." 'Protective measures' Hannigan said the damage left the club "frantically" trying to rearrange plans with the other clubs and Blackpool and District Youth Football League officials to avoid cancelling the games altogether. "They potentially deprived young sports people the chance to play the game they love," she said. "It caused major disruption because the games have had to be played elsewhere. "There is no way the damaged pitch can be played on in that state." It is understood Lancashire Police are investigating the incident, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said. Looking to the future, Bispham Junior Football Federation said it was liaising with landowners Blackpool Council to see if security measures at the pitches could be bolstered. "We'd like some kind of protective measures, possibly fencing or boulders, to make it more difficult to get vehicles on the pitches," Hannigan said. Deputy leader of Blackpool Council Jane Hugo said the authority was working with police to identify those involved. item.title: Former national champion amateur boxer Joscelyn Olayo-Munoz turning pro
item.description: Las Cruces standout boxer Joscelyn Olayo-Munoz is set to make her much-anticipated professional debut. The 19-year-old Olayo-Munoz will fight Dec. 17 in Colorado Springs, Colo., on a Ghost Town Promoted card. Olayo-Munoz will fight her first pro fight in the minimumweight division of 102 pounds in a four round fight. No opponent has been announced. "I can't wait to get going in my pro career, I'm ready," Olayo-Munoz said. "It's my goal to be a world champion and I learned so much as an amateur to get to this point." Olayo-Munoz was a 17-time national champion a nd represented the United States in international competition, where she won on that level as well. Olayo-Munoz also served as a team captain for Team USA. "Joscelyn is ready and she has so much potential moving forward," said Danny Melendrez, who is Olayo-Munoz's coach and stepfather. "She has a great passion for the sport." Felix F. item.title: Man United Women make it 12 unbeaten with comfortable 2-0 win over Crystal Palace
item.description: Man United Women make it 12 unbeaten with comfortable 2-0 win over Crystal Palace Manchester United Women welcomed Crystal Palace to the Progress with Unity Stadium. First half Elisabeth Terland had the hosts’ first chance, but her effort from distance sailed over the bar. Phallon Tullis-Joyce had to pull off an impressive stop to keep her side level at the near post. Terland broke through and put the ball past the keeper, but it was ruled out for offside. The Norwegian was close again, but her effort trickled just wide of the post. Finally, Manchester United captain Maya Le Tissier broke the deadlock. Manchester United midfielder Jess Park picked out Le Tissier, who smashed a strike into the bottom corner from 25 yards to perfectly mark her 150th match as a Red Devil. Jess Park, Julia Zigiotti and Simi Awujo all went close to scoring, but the Palace defence held firm and made an impressive stop on each occasion. Second half Palace started the second half with vigour, and Bethany England went close with a shot, but it trickled just wide of the goal. Le Tissier flicked the ball towards goal, but her effort went just wide. In the 65th minute, United made the game much more comfortable when they scored their second. Park played in Elisabeth Terland , and she kept her cool to slot the ball past the Palace keeper. The game became more transitional, and Lea Schüller almost added a third, but her shot went just over the crossbar. The match petered out in a 2-0 win, and Eva Olid’s side made it 12 matches unbeaten in all competitions. United now find themselves fourth and just one point behind the Champions League places and London City Lionesses. Man United Women results 26/27 Featured image by Ben Roberts Photo via Getty Images

item.description: ‘Everything a coach wants:’ UGA football commit dies after medical emergency Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School A Georgia high school community is mourning the loss of a standout student-athlete who was preparing to take the next step toward his dream of playing college football. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Marcellus Young Casario, known to friends and teammates as “Mar,” died after a sudden medical emergency, Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School announced Saturday. Casario was a boarding student who came to the Rabun Gap school from Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada, as a junior. He quickly became a beloved member of the campus community, where he was known as a natural leader, loyal friend and dedicated student-athlete. A standout defensive lineman, Casario had committed to play football at the University of Georgia, school officials said. He was looking forward to graduating from Rabun Gap in December and enrolling at UGA in January, according to school officials. His love for football started at an early age, inspired by his father and grandfather, who helped foster his passion for the game. He often encouraged others and shared his faith with those around him. “Mar brought light, faith, and character to everything he did, and his absence is a tremendous void in our close-knit community,” Head of School Bob Ahrens said. Ahrens said the school’s thoughts and prayers are with Casario’s family in Halifax, as well as his teammates and friends. Rabun Gap said it is providing counseling, spiritual support and other care services for students, faculty and staff as they grieve. The school asked the public to respect the privacy of Casario’s family. [SIGN UP: WSB-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

The reporter relied on AI search results for a statistic about Gilgeous-Alexander’s first-half assists, only for the two-time MVP to point out the mistake. During a press conference , the reporter asked Gilgeous-Alexander about recording assists in the first half of his previous game. The guard quickly corrected him, explaining that he had finished the first half against the Portland Trail Blazers without an assist. However, the reporter acknowledged that the figure came from an AI search, while also laughing off the risks of relying on generated answers without checking the underlying statistics. The moment came during a difficult stretch for Oklahoma City. The Thunder recently suffered a 113-112 loss to the LA Clippers, extending their losing streak to three games for the first time in more than three years. Gilgeous-Alexander still delivered an outstanding performance , scoring 40 points on 15-of-26 shooting while adding five assists and four rebounds. He also had two opportunities to win the game in the final seconds, but neither attempt found the basket. The two-time MVP has been carrying a heavy offensive burden amid Oklahoma City’s injury problems. His performance against the Clippers showed that he can still produce at an elite level, even when the supporting cast is depleted. item.title: FIU at Delaware in Conference USA football | Live report, updates
item.description: The Blue Hens will hope their preparation pays off at Delaware Stadium on Nov. 14, knowing that will be among a multitude of requirements needed to prevail. Their 2026 football season may be riding on it. Delaware (4-5 overall, 2-3) and Florida International (4-5, 2-3) kick off at 3 p.m. in the Conference USA game. A large Homecoming Day crowd is expected for the Blue Hens’ first Saturday home game since Sept. 19. It is being streamed on ESPN+. With a road game at New Mexico State next weekend and a season finale against Conference USA co-leader Jacksonville State looming, Delaware’s six-win bowl eligibility is in jeopardy. “Every team is good in this conference,” said Blue Hens running back Viron Ellison Jr. “We really have to prep well and it really starts Sundays after we play our game on Saturday, with recovery and mindset in preparing for the next game.” Delaware will see today if it has done what it needs to thwart the Panthers, who’ll be playing with the same desperation and determination. A frustrating 42-40 loss last week at Kennesaw State likely provided Ellison and his teammates with plenty of motivation. The Blue Hens will be looking to limit the explosive plays that have hurt them defensively while getting their offense moving against one of CUSA’s stingier units. The games matches a Delaware offense that is second in CUSA in yards per game against an FIU unit that’s second in total defense. “They're really good,” Delaware coach Ryan Carty said of the Panthers. “They pass rush really well. That’s what starts it all. Their front is extremely good. They're statistically great, but they're talented. They're not just good against the pass. They play physical in the run game. They're stout. They can hold up.” FIU’s secondary is also quite adept, Carty added, meaning quarterback Nick Minicucci will have to be on target and Delaware receivers must win their one-one-one confrontations.” “They can go make a play in some wide spaces,” Carty said, “and so we got our work cut out for us for sure.” Contact Kevin Tresolini at ktresolini@delawareonline.com and follow on Twitter @kevintresolini. item.title: How Austin Championship trophy was forged with bats, Moonlight Towers and Texas steel
item.description: AUSTIN, Texas — At their East Austin shop, Zach Henke and Justus Cogdell are used to working with steel. Big steel. Their day-to-day work includes everything from structural I-beams and cranes to custom staircases, railings and decorative vent hoods. But recently, an unexpected email brought a project unlike anything they had done before: building the trophy for the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions . And the pair had to do it quickly. Tournament organizers needed a late replacement after plans for another trophy fell through, so they reached out to Henke and his team to see what they could come up with on a tight deadline. "You just don't get opportunities every day to build something like this," Henke said. Fortunately, Henke had the right guy in the shop. More: Austin Championship merchandise gets Texas makeover after Good Good sponsorship fallout Cogdell, Henke's shop manager, is also a trained blacksmith. While plenty of people spend their free time playing golf, Cogdell spends his at the forge. He got into blacksmithing at Austin Community College, where he completed a two-year specialization in sculptural blacksmithing. Since then, the craft has been his job, his hobby and, at times, a side hustle. Now he was being asked to make his first championship trophy. Organizers didn't give them many restrictions. They provided the tournament logo and asked that a bat somehow be incorporated into the trophy. Beyond that, Henke and Cogdell had room to get creative. For Cogdell, who grew up in Austin, that meant making sure there was no mistaking where the trophy came from. He sketched out a design incorporating the city's historic Moonlight Towers, then turned the requested bat into a Mexican free-tailed bat, the species famous for the massive colony that lives beneath the Congress Avenue Bridge. More: 2026 Austin Championship leaderboard, live scores, tee times, projected standings The result is a trophy loaded with Austin touches. Getting it finished, however, has turned into a race against the clock. "It's extremely fun. I love creative projects and sculpture," Cogdell said. "It was a little stressful because the timeline's really tight, but being able to go through the creative process and think about what we want to incorporate and how to make it unique to Austin, which I grew up in, was really, really fun." Cogdell has made plenty of sculptural pieces over the years, but never anything quite like this. With the Austin Championship underway, he and Henke are relishing the attention that came from a trophy that started with little more than an email, a tournament logo and a request for a bat. Soon enough, somebody at Omni Barton Creek Resort will hoist it. Tim Schmitt is the managing editor of Golfweek and the golf coordinator of the USA Today Network. item.title: Matt Jung injury update, Wisconsin safety carted off field vs Maryland
item.description: The Wisconsin football team has lost another one of its key defensive players to an injury. Starting safety Matt Jung exited Wisconsin's Week 11 game against Maryland on Saturday, Nov. 14, with an apparent leg injury at the end of the second quarter. The UW training staff used an air cast and carted him off the field after spending significant time on the field tending to the injury. Matt Jung injury Jung suffered the injury while making a play that realistically saved at least three points for the Badgers . Maryland had first-and-goal on Wisconsin 's 1-yard line, but then Maryland quarterback Cardell Williams fumbled the ball and Jung recovered it. Who is Matt Jung? Jung, a fifth-year safety from Neenah, has played a crucial role on the Badgers' 2026 defense. He started in every game and ranked third on the team with 64 tackles before the Maryland game, trailing only linebackers Cooper Catalano and Mason Posa. Wisconsin football injury update It was part of a rough first half for the Badgers from an injury standpoint. Posa visited the medical tent before coming back into the game. Arizona State transfer cornerback Javan Robinson also went down with an injury and was helped off the field. Those injuries are in addition to Sebastian Cheeks' injury in practice this week , which kept him out of the Maryland game. Check back later for more updates. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Darian Mensah is one of the top quarterbacks in the country, but he’s already at his third school in three seasons. Mensah began his college football career as the QB for the Tulane Green Wave. His play there earned him a big contract with the Duke Blue Devils. But after a year in Durham, a late transfer portal entry and a lawsuit, Mensah landed with the Miami Hurricanes for the 2026 season. Miami is a top-10 team, coming off its first loss of the season (at Notre Dame), and will take on Duke on Saturday. Mensah will be in the spotlight even more than usual. The 8-1 Hurricanes host the 7-2 Blue Devils in a game with intriguing ACC implications. Miami still doesn’t have Malachi Toney, making things a bit tougher on them. item.title: Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria? Dana White Likes the Idea of It
item.description: Paddy Pimblett Ilia Topuria Dana White Getty UFC president Dana White said that he likes the idea of a lightweight bout between two of his biggest stars, Ilia Topuria and Paddy Pimblett. Topuria is set to return to the UFC Octagon in early 2027, and he has been connected to a matchup against Pimblett, his long-time rival. It seems like White, the one who makes the ultimate decision about what big fights the UFC books, likes the sound of this matchup. Dana White Likes a Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria Fight Speaking to Bleacher Report, White said he would be down for Pimblett vs. Topuria. “Paddy Pimblett versus Ilia Topuria is a huge fight that makes sense and can happen and should happen. Those are the kind of fights I like talking about,” White said. 🚨Dana White says Ilia Topuria vs. Paddy Pimblett is a “HUGE FIGHT” that can and should happen. “Paddy Pimblett versus Ilia Topuria is a huge fight that makes sense and can happen and should happen. Those are the kind of fights I like talking about.” pic.twitter.com/59j6hZwMlx — Red Corner MMA (@RedCorner_MMA) November 14, 2026 Fight Makes Sense A lightweight bout between Pimblett and Topuria makes too much sense, so hopefully, the UFC gets this fight booked as soon as possible. These are two of the top lightweights in the sport right now; neither of them has a fight booked, and both of them hate each other. So, it just makes a ton of sense for this fight to get booked as soon as possible. The UFC has begun booking its fights for early 2027, and a matchup between Pimblett and Topuria would be the perfect main event for a numbered UFC event. Even if there is no belt on the line between these two, they are still two of the biggest names in the sport, and the promotion could easily justify a numbered card for the pair. So, we’ll see what happens here, but given that White seems more than thrilled with the idea of these two stepping into the Octagon against each other and scrapping, it does feel like there is very real momentum building towards the UFC booking these two against each other. If they do end up fighting, look for the fight to potentially take place in March or April as the main event of the UFC’s numbered events in either of those months, with Las Vegas, Nevada, and Phoenix, Arizona, mentioned as possible locations. item.title: Arizona men’s cross country advances to NCAA Championships
item.description: For the first time in two decades, the Arizona men’s cross country team will be competing at the NCAA Championships. The Wildcats men advanced to next week’s national championship meet by finishing in fifth place at the NCAA West Regional on Friday. The showing was enough for Arizona to earn an at-large berth. Arizona last competed at NCAA Championships in 2006. The team took 21st place that year. Evans Tanui led Arizona on Friday with a 6th place individual finish, running a 10K time of 29:13.4. Josphat Meli took 19th with a time of 29:37.4, and Vincent Gwachi took 27th with a time of 29:50.6. Lawi Ngetich and Hanibal Haile rounded out Arizona’s five scorers. All-Region Honors for Evans Tanui! ⏱️6th Place – 29:13.4 #BearDown pic.twitter.com/7Qly8cLMDd — Arizona Track & Field/Cross Country (@ArizonaTrack) November 13, 2026 Arizona finished in a tie with Portland with 141 points, but Portland won the tiebreaker by way of total time it took its athletes to cross the finish line. Oregon won the race, followed by Washington and Stanford. On the women’s side, freshman Mercy Chepkemoi put together another standout performance, finishing runner-up in the 6K with a time of 18:59.o. By placing in the top four, Chepkemoi qualified for the NCAA Championships. All-Region Honors for Mercy Chepkemoi! ⏱️2nd Place – 18:59.0 #BearDown pic.twitter.com/ZTV6jnKeLn — Arizona Track & Field/Cross Country (@ArizonaTrack) November 13, 2026 Praise Chepkemoi finished in 10th place with a time of 19:48.5, earning her All-Region Honors. The Arizona women as a team finished in 11th place, their best showing at the West Regional since 2013. The NCAA Championships will be held Nov. 21 in Terre Haute, Ind.

item.title: International round-up: Haaland on target in important Norway win over Wales
item.description: International round-up: Haaland on target in important Norway win over Wales Erling Haaland scored the decisive third goal as Norway defeated Wales 3-1 in UEFA National League qualifying. RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa opened the scoring just before the hour mark with Andreas Schjelderup doubling the advantage for the hosts shortly after at Ullevaal Stadion, Haaland setting up the Benfica winger for the second goal. David Brooks pulled one back for Craig Bellamy’s men but Haaland put the contest beyond The Dragons by despatching a penalty late on after playing in Schjelderup who was fouled by Connor Roberts. The City hitman made no mistake from the spot to bring up his 66th goal for Norway. The result moved Stale Solbakken’s men up to second in League A - Group 4, six points behind leaders Portugal who host third place Denmark later this evening. The top two teams will advance to two‑legged quarter‑finals in March 2027 with the winners of those qualifying for the June 2027 Finals inclusive of semi‑finals, third‑place match and final. Portugal, two-time winners, are defending champions having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024/25 finals, held in Germany. In the early hours of the morning UK time, Enzo Fernández played 90 minutes for Argentina as they lost 2-1 at home to Uruguay in a friendly at Estadio Alberto José Armando. Leonardo Balerdi’s own-goal allied to Maximiliano Araújo’s effort put the visitors two-up only for former Blue, Julián Alvarez to reduce arrears but it was too little, too late as La Albiceleste fell to defeat. Vitor Reis was an unused substitute as Brazil went down 3-2 to Japan at the Singapore National Stadium. Goals from Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the hosts in control but the visitors came back strong courtesy of a Vinícius Júnior brace. But there was late drama with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto bundling home at the death, sparking red cards for manager Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha, the dismissals coming as a result of questioning why a foul hadn’t been given in favour of Joao Gomes in the build-up to that late winner. item.title: Cam Newton says he’s now changed his mind on the rule change coming into college football
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Cam Newton revealed that he has finally come around to accept the new 24-team playoff format in College Football Playoffs. It was confirmed that the CFP would have 24 teams, which is an increase of 12 from the previous format. There have been many critics of the new format, as they believed it would take away the heart and soul of college football, which is the conference championship game. However, Newton, who has had some of the most legendary College Football seasons, was willing to let go of that due to what it was bringing in. “Initially, I felt like this gentleman as well. I was so devastated man, I seen and looked at my threads. I looked at my Instagram. I said, oh man, that’s the death of the SEC Championship in Atlanta. SEC would no longer have a SEC Championship. Oh my goodness, the nostalgia of that in that December weekend. Oh my goodness. “But then I started to realize, I said, hold on. Let me dive a little deeper. I love it. Because the reality of it all is this. There would never be another undefeated college football team ever. Think about it. Throughout this format, teams get penalized for playing soft schedules. I like that. That’s all I wanted to see, I didn’t always have SEC bias, I didn’t necessarily care if it was big table, what I do care about is how did you get there? Now teams will be penalized for having a weakness in their schedule.” Newton was part of the SEC across his stints with the Florida Gators and Auburn. He knows how massive the conference championship games are, especially in the SEC. Newton himself had an iconic game in the Conference Championship game, where he scored 6 touchdowns to help Auburn advance to the National Championship game. The new format seems to not only help boost revenue for College Football, but also allow programs that have just missed out on the playoffs to make a push. In times where NIL is dominating the sport, the extra few spots for teams gives them a shot. item.title: Wales' top-tier survival hopes hit by Norway loss
item.description: Norway's win over Wales was only their second of this Nations League campaign [Getty Images] Wales' hopes of retaining their top-tier status in the Nations League are hanging in the balance after they were beaten by Norway in Oslo. Wales shaded a goalless first half in which they created the better chances, but Norway scored with their first shot on target as Antonio Nusa drilled in from the edge of the penalty area after an hour. The World Cup quarter-finalists doubled their lead nine minutes later as Nusa and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland combined for substitute Andreas Schjelderup to tap in. Wales kept themselves in the contest as David Brooks came off the bench to score with a delicate chipped finish, only for Haaland's penalty to wrap up victory for the hosts after Schjelderup was fouled by Connor Roberts. By avenging their defeat in Cardiff a month ago, Norway leapfrog Wales into third place in Group A4, meaning Craig Bellamy's side will finish bottom. Even if they win their final game at home to group leaders and reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday, Wales cannot overtake Norway or Denmark – who are both three points ahead – because of their inferior head-to-head record. As a result, they are almost certain to face a relegation play-off against a League B team in March. More to follow. [Getty Images]

item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - FEBRUARY 03: Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles speaks to the media during Super Bowl LIX Opening Night at Caesars Superdome on February 03, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Makai Lemon #9 and Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrate after Goedert's receiving touchdown against the Washington Commanders in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni high fives Dallas Goedert #88 before a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty Most expected Dallas Goedert to be traded by the Philadelphia Eagles at the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Once the deadline went into effect, it was clear that he would finish the season in Philadelphia. Once again, Goedert was at risk of leaving, but the Eagles decided to keep him around. It wasn’t due to a total lack of interest. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, “several teams” inquired about the availability of the veteran tight end. Which team was mentioned? The San Francisco 49ers. Eagles Star Dallas Goedert Landed Trade Interest From 49ers Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – SEPTEMBER 13: Makai Lemon #9 and Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrate after Goedert’s receiving touchdown against the Washington Commanders in the fourth quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Schefter stated that while the 49ers inquired, discussions never got close. It’s unclear why. While the general manager, Howie Roseman, has been criticized for setting high prices for trade candidates over the past year (Tanner McKee was a good example), the Eagles’ interest in potentially retaining Goedert for another year could’ve played into their decision to keep him around. According to Schefter, Goedert “could even re-sign with the Eagles for 2027.” That feels like a “wink-wink” hint at the tight end’s upcoming free agency. item.title: De la Fuente feels the strain as Lamine Yamal club v country debate rages in Spain
item.description: Head coach hits out at ‘lies’ as suggestions of preferential treatment for young star overshadow preparations for England game in Madrid From the London Palladium to Madrid’s Metropolitano, they’re all here. On Sunday night, the footballers who lifted the game’s biggest awards meet again three weeks later and on the field this time, dinner jackets but not a single man left behind. Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or and Gerd Müller trophy winner. Unai Simón, holder of the Lev Yashin award . Luis de la Fuente , the coach of the year who on Thursday night announced that also joining them will be Lamine Yamal , the kid who lifted the Kopa award as the best young player for the third year running and said he would have preferred Pau Cubarsí to be standing there instead. And, yes, Cubarsí will be there too for the final Nations League group game. At 1.45pm on Friday the world and European champions landed back at Madrid’s Barajas airport from Prague, where they had won again, before making their way by bus to their Las Rozas HQ, around the M40 motorway to the north-west of the capital. At about the same time, Lamine Yamal arrived from Barcelona, due in at midday. As was Mikel Oyarzabal , scorer of the winner at Euro 2024 and Spain’s top marksman this summer (not that he would ever tell you so) from San Sebastián. At 7.30pm, they trained, preparing to meet the World Cup semi-finalists and the team they defeated in Berlin at the end of Euro 2024. Two starters from the World Cup final will be absent: Dani Olmo and the captain, 2024 Ballon d’Or winner Rodri , are injured. But everyone else will be there. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Taking a brief minute to remember Pierre Sage’s impact at Crystal Palace
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! So farewell then, Pierre Sage . Many coaches leave under a cloud, not many have their departures completely obscured by the foul, retch-inducing one emanating from another team’s managerial circus, but such was Sage’s fate . The news section of Crystal Palace’s website helpfully tells you the amount of time it might take you to read each story it links through to. For example it should take four minutes or so to get through Tuesday’s “On this day: five big Crystal Palace birthdays”. “England: I love a knee slide!” will take you five. “Prize draw: be a mascot for our next [Bigger Vase] tie!” is a two-minute job. The statement informing the world of Sage’s exit? One minute. Eighty-three words. By way of illustration, the word “words” was the 84th of this paragraph. Just because the man’s French doesn’t mean his exit should be marked with a shrug. As I have been away at a conference, giving a presentation that the MC described as ‘sobering’, I’ve missed the last few days of football, so I was very sad to read about the passing of the great Danny Kelly . Others are far better placed to give tributes to the great man, but for younger generations who can’t comprehend the football cultural significance, Baker and Kelly represented the peak of football phone-ins. Before it became people ranting and raving about wanting the manager sacked as they’ve lost a few games or wanting the club to spend another few hundred million pounds on yet more players, it was about football supporters and supporting, from fans who actually went to games. Their peak was on BBC Radio in the 1990s, and there are too many examples of their greatness, but if I had to pick one, just one to illustrate it, it would, of course, be Gordon the Dundee United supporter and his bow tie . Rest in Peace, Danny Kelly. You gave us such joy” – Noble Francis. As they no longer seem to be ‘Dr Tottenham’, I was wondering if they had maybe passed the soubriquet on. I think the England cricket team has provided the answer (again)” – Andrew Parker. Impressive list of kiss-off press releases ( yesterday’s Football Daily ) but why was Ralf Rangnick omitted from the chronological list of post-Fergie managers? Is it because Football Daily valued him as little as Manchester United fans did?” – Mike Wilner. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
item.description: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revival It may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists. The Italian Futurist Umberto Boccioni whirled an athlete’s body into a vortex of movement in his 1913 painting Dynamism of a Soccer Player . You can see one of the earliest fine art depictions of a match – a smoggy, factory-adjactent scene called Any Wintry Afternoon in England – at the Manchester Art Gallery. If 1930s abstraction is more your thing, you can enjoy decoding the geometric shapes in Kazimir Malevich’s Painterly Realism of a Football Player – Color Masses in the 4th Dimension. I’m guessing the small green pea shape is a ball. These, in any case, were exceptions. In 1953 the Football Assocition launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park. An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the Football Association secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
